title: Infinite loop
body:
A loop that never stops, because nothing changes its [[Control variable]] or the condition can
never become false. Usually a [[Logic Errors|logic error]]: the update line is missing, or it
updates the wrong variable.

```c++
int i = 0;
while (i < 10)
	cout << i;      // i never changes
```

`ctrl + c` kills it. Occasionally deliberate (`while (true)` with a `break` inside), but not in
this course. The opposite is a [[Finite loop]].

Unbounded [[Recursion]] looks like the same mistake and is not: it crashes with a stack
overflow instead of spinning forever, because every call consumes stack. See
[[Stack and Heap]].
